gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.backoff_max: Idle backoff cap: ×%s (first item after idle waits up to %s extra cycles)
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.backoff_off: Idle backoff: OFF (default · identical to vanilla)
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.backoff_on: Idle backoff: ON (saves TPS on idle factories)
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.desc_backoff_1: Idle managers stretch their timer interval step by step and resume on the first successful transfer; average transfer rate per second is unchanged and redstone triggers are unaffected
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.desc_backoff_2: Only active when idle backoff is on; higher values save more while idle but lengthen first-item latency
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.desc_budget: Triggers over budget are deferred to the next tick (nothing moves = lost throughput!); enable only to protect TPS on heavily loaded servers
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.desc_default: Everything off by default = identical to vanilla SFM (throughput and first-item latency unchanged)
gui.sfmfactorystudio.tps.title: SFM Factory Studio · Server TPS Settings
sfmfactorystudio.configuration.enableIdl: Stretches timer intervals step by step while a manager keeps moving nothing; any successful move resets instantly. Default off = identical to vanilla SFM (including first-item latency after idle). Enable only on high-load servers; average throughput is unchanged and redstone triggers are unaffected.
sfmfactorystudio.configuration.maxIdleBa: Only used when idle backoff is enabled. The first item of an idle factory may wait up to (multiplier-1) extra intervals.
sfmfactorystudio.configuration.tickBudge: Caps total per-tick time of all managers; over-budget runs are deferred this tick. Deferred runs move nothing = throughput loss! Keep 0 = off (default); enable only on dying servers where survival matters more than throughput.
